lines.en: What is written on this small clay tablet?
A story? A king's name?
No. It is an account kept by people about 5,000 years ago.
Around 3200 BCE.
Uruk, in southern Mesopotamia.
One of the largest early cities in the world.
The city is growing. Farming, trade and administration are becoming more complex.
Grain, livestock, workers and goods...
Large institutions had to manage them all.
Who received how much grain? How much arrived? How much remained?
Keeping all of this in memory alone was not easy.
No paper. No books.
Long before coins, people in Uruk kept records by pressing marks into clay.
The quantity and details of every item were recorded in marks.
Many of the earliest tablets found at Uruk are administrative records.
How much grain was there? Who delivered it? How much was handed out?
The same number sign could stand for different quantities, depending on what was being counted.
But many of the tablets we study today were not found in carefully kept collections.
They had been thrown away, and later buried in building fill.
Thousands of years later, they came to light again.
One group of signs appears in an ancient account...
"KU.ŠIM".
Was it a person's name? A title? Or the name of an institution?
Even after 5,000 years, the question remains unresolved.
